sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX draft; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: \textbf{Choose the axis}\par About the \(x\)-axis: integrate \(\pi y^2\) with respect to \(x\).\par About the \(y\)-axis: integrate \(\pi x^2\) with respect to \(y\).
\textbf{Choose the method}\par Convert limits when using a parameter.\par Subtract inner volumes for hollow regions.\par Apply cubic scale factors to volumes in models.

slides.title: Volumes of Revolution with harder integration

transcription.tex: The region under \(y=\sin2x\), from \(x=0\) to \(x=\pi/2\), is rotated about the \(x\)-axis. Find its volume.
A thin disc has radius \(y\) and thickness \(dx\).\[dV=\pi y^2dx,\qquad V=\pi\int_a^b y^2dx\]

transcription.tex: 3. The region bounded by \(y=\ln x\), the \(x\)-axis and \(x=3\) is rotated about the \(x\)-axis. Find its exact volume.
The curve meets the axis at \(x=1\). Integrate by parts twice:\[V=\pi\int_1^3(\ln x)^2dx\]\[=\pi[x(\ln x)^2-2x\ln x+2x]_1^3\]\[=\pi(3(\ln3)^2-6\ln3+4)\]

transcription.tex: Challenge. Rotate the region between \(y=\sin x\) and \(y=1/\sqrt2\), for \(\pi/4\le x\le3\pi/4\), about the line \(y=1/\sqrt2\). Find the exact volume.
The radius is the distance above the rotation axis:\[V=\pi\int_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4}(\sin x-1/\sqrt2)^2dx\]\[=\pi[x-\sin2x/4+\sqrt2\cos x]_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4}\]\[=\frac\pi2(\pi-3)\]

transcription.tex: 8a. Prove \(\sin^5\theta=(10\sin\theta-5\sin3\theta+\sin5\theta)/16\).\par b. Rotate the region between \(x=\sin^2y\sqrt{\sin y}\) and the \(y\)-axis, \(\pi/4\le y\le\pi\). Find the exact volume.
Writing \(s=\sin\theta\), use \(\sin3\theta=3s-4s^3\) and \(\sin5\theta=5s-20s^3+16s^5\); eliminate \(s^3\) and rearrange.

\[a=4,\quad V=\pi\int x^2dy\]Use only the right-hand half: rotating it already generates the whole solid.

transcription.tex: A goldfish bowl is modelled by rotating \(x=2\sin t,\ y=2\cos t+2\), \(\pi/6\le t\le11\pi/6\), about the \(y\)-axis.\par a. Find the volume up to height 3 cm.\par b. A similar real bowl has maximum diameter 48 cm. Find the corresponding water volume.
The model maximum diameter is 4 cm; linear scale factor is 12.\[V_{\rm real}=12^3(9\pi)=15552\pi\approx48900\ \mathrm{cm}^3\]

Show \(x^2=\frac{16}{81}y^2(9-y^2)\).\par b. Find the maximum number made from \(300\ \mathrm{mm}^3\) of silver.\par c. Discuss modelling limitations.
A patterned or hollow earring may use less silver; loss during casting may reduce the number made.
